100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On August 5, 1926, the British General Strike entered its final week, with tensions rising as negotiations between labor unions and the government continued to falter. In the United States, a surge in summer heat prompted warnings of heat-related illnesses across several states. Meanwhile, in Egypt, King Fuad I announced plans for constitutional reforms, aiming to stabilize the nation's political landscape. The international community remained watchful as these developments unfolded, reflecting the era's ongoing social and political upheavals.
